Q1.answer: The source card asked: "Does feeding many GPUs to the block-tridiagonal Newton solve shorten its depth from T ordered steps to log2(T)?" (../20261019-2344-tree/out/RESULT.md). The run turns this into the card's own decision rule: lever only if parallel cyclic reduction beats one-thread Thomas by at least 2 times at 2^24 equations, and the speedup grows with size (QUESTION.md). An answer is the verdict of that rule, together with the numbers the card promised to measure later (RUN.md).

Q2.answer: The runner generated tridiagonal systems from fixed seeds, with a diagonal of 3 and off-diagonals of plus or minus 1, in double precision (QUESTION.md). It timed five sizes from 2^10 to 2^24 equations, on five seeds each (QUESTION.md). The box was one rented 40 GB data-centre GPU at 1.99 dollars an hour (RUN.md). The measurement code is one Python runner and one shell script that runs its stages on the box (run_m2.py) (onbox_m2.sh).

Q3.answer: The deciding baseline is the card's own: a hand-written Thomas kernel with one GPU thread per system (results_m2/out/records/id-E3_kind-endpoint_run-m2.json). The run's write-up calls that the slowest sensible way to run Thomas (TAKEAWAYS_m2.md). In practice a scientist would use a CPU library routine or the vendor's GPU solver. The operator added one CPU core running the LAPACK routine through scipy as a report-only floor, which took a median 416.7 ms at 2^24 equations (results_m2/out/records/id-E7_kind-endpoint_run-m2.json).

Q4.answer: At 2^24 equations the parallel solver took a median 21.8 ms against 7598.5 ms for one GPU thread, a speedup of 348.3 (results_m2/out/records/id-E3_kind-endpoint_run-m2.json). The speedups at the five sizes were 8.54, 95.90, 517.53, 395.38 and 348.30, with a fitted slope of 0.256 (results_m2/out/records/id-E3_kind-endpoint_run-m2.json). The lower quartile across seeds at 2^24 was 348.29, so the spread is small (results_m2/out/records/id-E3_kind-endpoint_run-m2.json). Against one CPU core the speedup at 2^24 was 19.1 (results_m2/out/records/id-E7_kind-endpoint_run-m2.json). The number counts under the card's rule of at least 2 times with growth (QUESTION.md).

Q5.answer: Before timing, both hand-written solvers had to reach a relative residual of at most 1e-10 and agree within 1e-8 with the vendor GPU solver and with scipy, at 2^10 and 2^14 equations (results_m2/out/records/id-E1_kind-endpoint_run-m2.json). Both passed (results_m2/out/records/id-E1_kind-endpoint_run-m2.json). The largest relative residual of either solver was 3.11e-16 (results_m2/out/records/id-E2_kind-endpoint_run-m2.json).

Q6.answer: Twelve predictions with probabilities were sealed and hashed before any agent or box ran (SEALED_PREDICTIONS.md). Ten held and two did not occur, for a Brier score of 0.090 (out/PREDICTIONS_SCORED.md). The forecast that the parallel solver would come within 3 times of the vendor solver failed: it was 7.4 times slower (out/PREDICTIONS_SCORED.md). Among the card's own guesses, the measured speedup was 12.44 times its proxy of 28 (results_m2/out/records/id-E5_kind-endpoint_run-m2.json).

Q7.answer: Nothing was voided, and every planted control passed (TAKEAWAYS_m2.md). The optional block and multi-GPU phases of the card were not run, by an operator decision before launch (RUN.md). The isolated reader in triage did not run because its agent type was not found (RUN.md). None of these touches the timed comparison that answers the question.

Q8.answer: The answer covers one GPU model, double precision, the generated diagonally dominant systems, and sizes from 2^10 to 2^24 equations (QUESTION.md). The timed blocks repeat solves on data already on the GPU, so copies from the host are not in the times (TAKEAWAYS_m2.md). Nothing above 2^24 equations, no other GPU and no real Newton system was measured (QUESTION.md).

Q9.answer: The box ran one launch of 0.239 hours at 1.99 dollars an hour, 0.48 dollars in total (RUN.md). The box was billed 4.80 dollars for the launch (RUN.md). The sweep itself took 0.119 hours against the card's planned need of 2 hours (results_m2/out/records/id-E10_kind-endpoint_run-m2.json). The run had a hard cap of 8 dollars and at most two launches (RUN.md). Running it again needs the same rented GPU, the runner and the on-box script (onbox_m2.sh).

Q10.answer: On this GPU the parallel solver is about 19.1 times faster than one CPU core at 2^24 equations, which is the comparison a practitioner needs (results_m2/out/records/id-E7_kind-endpoint_run-m2.json). The write-up asks next for a case with the data copied to the GPU as well as one with the data resident (TAKEAWAYS_m2.md). A second run on a newer GPU would double the speedup (TAKEAWAYS_m2.md).
